Comment: ALBION: THE BEST MMOPRG IN THE WORLD!   Thank you SBI, long life for Albion!   Now, my SUGGESTION for the future hahaha:  [SUGGESTION] Mount Food, Hydration, and Interaction System  Executive Summary:  1. Introduction: Active Hunger and Thirst system for mounts while equipped/in use.  2. Economic Integration: Mount food crafted by players using Island resources and crafting stations.  3. Utility & Buffs: Dynamic consumables that boost the economy without breaking PvP balance.  4. Immersion & Animations: Open-world hydration mechanics and direct player-mount interactions.  Context:  In the world of Albion Online, mounts are essential — exploring this massive universe would be impossible without them. The fact that mounts are raised and saddled by the players themselves is one of the coolest mechanics in the game. However, once an animal is saddled and ready for use, all interaction regarding "caring" for your companion completely ceases.  This proposal aims to bring immersion, functionality, and economic value to Albion Online by introducing a lightweight mount maintenance system.  1. Hunger and Thirst System How It Works: Mounts will feature Hunger and Thirst meters that decay only while equipped and in active use in the open world. While stored in banks, chests, or inventory, consumption is paused (though the mount's current stats are saved).  Consumption & Penalties: Consumption rate should be balanced and predictable. There are no progressive debuffs: if the meter drops to 0%, a flat penalty is applied (such as reduced movement speed or decreased carry capacity). Attacks received by the mount do not affect the hunger/thirst meters.  Battle Mounts: Battle Mounts have a higher food consumption rate and are strictly limited to Tier 1 food.  2. Open-World Hydration Simple & Free Mechanics:  Hydration incurs no costs and occurs naturally during exploration.  How It Works: Approaching rivers or lakes in the Open World, Mists, or Roads of Avalon unlocks an option for the mount to drink water and satisfy its thirst, complete with a new drinking animation. (Feature unavailable in ocean water).  3. Mount Food & Economy (Crafting & Buffs): Mount food will be consumable items freely tradeable on the Market, crafted at city stations using player Island crops and ingredients.  Tier 1: Satisfies mount hunger only. (The only food permitted for Battle Mounts).  Tier 3: Satisfies hunger and restores 20% of the mount's HP (Out-of-Combat only, 10s cooldown).  Tier 5: Satisfies hunger and grants a 5% bonus based on the mount's main archetype: Transport & Gathering Mounts: +5% Carry Capacity (direct and stackable bonus). Speed & Mobility Mounts: +5% Flat Movement Speed (Example: A Swiftclaw running at 120% becomes 125%; a Direwolf running at 132% becomes 137%).  4. Animations and Interactivity To enhance roleplay and immersion, players (whether mounted or dismounted) gain new options to interact directly with their mount via emotes or context menus:  Petting the mount;  Adjusting the saddle / inspecting the animal's packs and gear;

Core Argument: Praising the game and pitching an elaborate mount hunger, hydration, and interaction system.

Comment: The Ancient Lands portal system is extremely frustrating. We wait for almost an hour just for the portal to appear. Wait for an hour, gather our group, enter the portal, and die within seconds without even getting a chance to play the content? This system feels like a waste of players' time. Small groups have almost no chance when a massive group is camping the portal. We don't even get to experience the Ancient Lands because we're killed before we can explore or do anything. Please seriously reconsider how the portals work. Add more portals, spread the entrances across different locations, increase the number of players that can enter, or provide some form of temporary protection when entering. Ancient Lands could be great content, but right now the portal system is making it almost impossible for smaller groups to enjoy it.
